messages:
maya: quick sync — last night at ~00:42 UTC we had a ~3min latency spike in us-west for hosted text-gen. customers hit error pages and our fallback path didn’t kick in reliably. i sketched a short PRD update + runbook delta, putting it here for review: https://notion.redwood/prd/latency-blip-2026

alex: saw the same in logs. root cause looks like a batching backlog + router healthcheck not triggering fallback. two quick engineering guardrails i propose:
- router: if request_queue > 500 for > 30s, route to 8-bit quant variant
- runtime: reduce max_batch_size to 32 when avg_latency > 400ms

sam-sre: +1 to both. need concrete SLOs and oncall playbook steps in PRD. my draft SLO (proposed): p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 1s for hosted gen under normal load. acceptance criteria should include automated canary verification and runbook-drill pass. also add an alert: queue_length > 400 for 2m => P1 pagerduty.

lauren-support: we had 4 enterprise tickets and one paid customer called in. include a customer-communication template in PRD and the escalation matrix (who to loop at 15/30/60 min). also mark which customers get proactive emails.

chao-ml: some edge cases to capture in the spec:
- very long prefixes (>8k tokens) blow up KV cache and trigger cascading latency; proposal: reject >8k tokens with 413 + body explaining token limit and compression tips
- metric to add: kv_cache_miss_rate and per-model avg_prefix_len
- fallback correctness: when routing to quant variant, ensure sampling seeds and deterministic choices match non-quant model within tolerance; add an offline eval to measure divergence <= 2% on eval set

maya: i’ll incorporate. for the runbook delta i sketched minimal steps so oncall can act fast:
1) triage: check `queue_length`, `backpressure_saturation`, `p95_latency` in console
2) if queue_length > 500 and p95 > 500ms -> enable router fallback (policy = `8bit_fallback`)
3) if after fallback p95 still > 1s for 5min -> scale up dedicated pool (or trigger emergency hot nodes) and notify customers
4) if scaling fails -> degrade non-critical features (embeddings/rerank) to free capacity and open incident bridge

example commands (for runbook):
```
# check queue length
curl -s https://infra-api.prod.redwood/v1/metrics?q=queue_length | jq .
# trigger fallback policy
curl -XPOST https://router-api.prod.redwood/v1/policies/fallback -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"policy":"8bit_fallback"}'
# scale up pool (requires infra perms)
curl -XPOST https://dedicated-api.prod.redwood/v1/pools/scale -d '{"pool":"us-west-hosted","delta":3}'
```

alex: for scope negotiation — recommend we split into two deliverables:
MVP (next 2 sprints): router guardrails + runbook steps + pager alerts + canary test harness
M1 (next quarter): dashboard surfaces (kv cache metrics, pref len), automatic rollback telemetry, customer comms templating integrated into console
who owns what? maya(PM) owner for PRD and comms; alex(eng) owner for router changes; sam-sre owns alerts/runbook drills; chao owns evals for quant divergence.

sam-sre: acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Canary: ramp to 10k requests with fallback exercised at least once and p95 <= 250ms during the canary window
- Runbook drill: oncall executes checklist in staging and confirms fallback triggers within 60s of simulated queue spike
- Alerts: queue_length > 400 for 2m triggers pager and auto-posts to #incidents with runbook link

lauren-support: add to PRD: customer comms checklist + recommended SLA language edits. also request a short FAQ for support agents (1-pager).

deploy-bot: new canary deploy succeeded 02:10 UTC — router v2.3.1 rolled to 10% traffic in us-west

maya: next steps — i'll update the PRD with the guardrails and the runbook delta and open an RFC for the router policy change. please review by EOD Friday. tagging owners: @alex @sam-sre @chao-ml @lauren-support. :eyes::thumbsup:

alex: will review. quick note — if we enable fallback on queue threshold we should also add a short cooldown (5m) to avoid flip-flopping when load oscillates. add that to the RFC.

chao-ml: noted on cooldown. i'll run the quant divergence eval and post numbers before the RFC review deadline.

sam-sre: scheduling a 30min runbook drill for Wed 16:00 UTC. will invite oncall and a support rep.

maya: thanks all — updating doc now: https://notion.redwood/prd/latency-blip-2026 (will link RFC once created)
